name: wyzie-mcp

tools.name: search_subtitles
tools.description: Search subtitles for a movie or episode by IMDb/TMDB id. Returns a compact JSON list (id, language, display, format, release, fileName, source, isHearingImpaired, downloadCount, match, quality, rank, url), best first: rank is {score 0-100, reasons} (100 minus penalties such as image_format, extra_file (a song, trailer or extra filed under the title), sdh, machine_translated, unreliable_source). Costs 1 request per source it runs (1 by default or with one source; source=all costs one per source the key may use). Pass a result's url to download_subtitle. Needs an API key.

id.description: IMDb id (tt0111161) or TMDB id (286217). Use search_tmdb to turn a title into an id.

season.description: Season number. Must be given together with episode.

episode.description: Episode number. Must be given together with season.

language.description: ISO 639-1 code, e.g. en, es. Comma separated for several (en,es).

format.description: srt, ass, vtt, sub... Comma separated for several.

source.description: Source codename(s), see list_sources. Default: charlie. all = every source the key may use (1 request each).

video.description: Video file name, e.g. Show.S02E03.1080p.WEB-DL-GROUP.mkv. Ranks results by fit and fills match.

hash.description: Movie hash (16 hex digits) of the video file.

sort.description: downloads: most downloaded first. quality: highest rank first, also with video/hash (which otherwise put the best release match first). Default: rank order.

tools.name: get_best_subtitle
tools.description: Get the single best subtitle for an id: text formats first, non hearing-impaired first (unless hi=true), never AI-generated. Returns one object or the text 'none'. Costs 1 request. Prefer this over search_subtitles when you only need one file.

hash.description: Movie hash (16 hex digits) of the video file.

sort.description: downloads: most downloaded first. quality: highest rank first, also with video/hash (which otherwise put the best release match first). Default: rank order.

tools.name: download_subtitle
tools.description: Download a subtitle's text from the url of a search result, optionally converting (to), shifting timing (offset/shift), fixing fps, stripping styling (plain), reflowing lines. Costs 1 request. Output is cut at 60000 characters.

url.description: The url field of a search_subtitles or get_best_subtitle result.

to.description: Output format. txt = text only, json = cues with seconds.

offset.description: Shift all cues by this many seconds (negative = earlier).

shift.description: Alias of offset: +2.5s, -1500ms, -00:00:02.500. Wins over offset.

plain.description: Strip styling codes, drop empty and repeated cues.

dual.description: ISO 639-1 code: add a second language under each line (Pro, +1 request).

lines.description: Reflow cues to at most this many characters per line.

maxlines.description: Max lines per cue when reflowing (default 2).

mindur.description: Minimum cue display time in seconds.

tools.name: get_subtitle_file
tools.description: One call: find the best subtitle for an id and return its text (GET /download). Costs 2 requests. Same search parameters as search_subtitles (language defaults to en) plus the download options. Returns the text plus the picked release, source and language.

tools.name: search_batch
tools.description: Search many titles in one call (1 to 50 items). Each item is an id (string or number) or an object with id, season, episode, language, format, source, hi, video, hash, sort, limit. Top-level language/format/source/hi/best are defaults. Costs the sum of its items, each priced as one search (1 request per source it runs). With best=true each item returns one subtitle or null.

best.description: true: only the best subtitle per item.

tools.name: search_quote
tools.description: Find the movie or episode a line of dialogue is said in. Returns up to 10 matches (imdbId, title, year, season, episode, timeMs, line, context). Costs 1 request.

tools.name: list_sources
tools.description: List the live subtitle sources (codenames usable as the source parameter) with tier and tags. With a key it also says which ones the key may use. Free.

tools.name: list_translation_languages
tools.description: List the languages AI translation can produce, as {code, name} pairs. Free, no key.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Wyzie Subs status and uptime: overall state, each source, uptime over 24h/7d/30d/90d, recent incidents. Free, no key.

days.description: Days of per-day history to include (default 0).

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Your key's balance, plan, daily usage and a per-day breakdown by route and source. Free (costs no requests). Needs a full key, not a browser key.

tools.name: search_tmdb
tools.description: Search TMDB by title to get the id for search_subtitles. Returns id, mediaType (movie or tv), title, releaseYear. Free, no key.

q.description: Title to look up, e.g. 'Breaking Bad'.

tools.name: extract_subtitles
tools.description: Pull embedded subtitle tracks out of a local video file (mkv, mp4, webm, mks...). Use list=true first to see the tracks (costs 1 request), then track or language to get one as text (1 request per track). Files up to 2 GB: over 100 MB the file is sent in resumable 8 MB chunks from disk first (paid keys). Image-based tracks (PGS, VobSub) cannot be extracted.

file_path.description: Absolute path of a local media file on this machine.

list.description: true: only list the tracks as JSON.

track.description: Subtitle stream number from the list.

language.description: ISO 639-1 or 639-2 code to pick the first text track in that language.

to.description: Output format. txt = text only, json = cues with seconds.

offset.description: Shift all cues by this many seconds (negative = earlier).

tools.name: transcribe_file
tools.description: Transcribe speech in a local audio or video file into subtitles. EXPENSIVE: costs 600 requests per started minute of audio (603 with speakers, plus 3 a file) and needs a Pro key. Waits until the job is done (can take minutes). Files up to 2 GB: over 100 MB the file is sent in resumable 8 MB chunks from disk first (sending audio only is cheaper to upload). Only use when the user asked for a transcription.

file_path.description: Absolute path of a local audio or video file.

speakers.description: Label speakers: 603 a minute instead of 600, plus 3 a file. Any language; language not needed. 503 before any charge when unavailable.

translate.description: Also translate into this language code (+1 request).

idempotency_key.description: Idempotency-Key for this job (1 to 100 letters, digits, _ . : -). Default: a random one per call. The same key again answers the first job (no second job, no second charge); 409 while the first still runs.

tools.name: censor_video_url
tools.description: Wyzie Censored (Pro): bleep, mute or cover chosen words in the video at a link (a media file, HLS, DASH or a page the server can read; up to 4 hours or 3 GB). PAID: 610 requests per started minute of media (recognition 600 + render 10; charged up front, the 600 refunded on a recognition cache hit, all of it if it fails on our side), or 1,925 with loud music mode (music: true; of the extra 1,315, the voices pass's 675 and the overlap pass's 640 are given back as far as the file doesn't need them: the job says music and overlap). Without confirm: true it only answers the exact price for this link and charges nothing; show it to the user, then call again with confirm: true. Starts a job: poll it with job_status (kind censor). Sites that block server fetching (such as YouTube) are refused before any charge: use the Wyzie browser extension there.

url.description: Public http(s) link to a video or audio.

language.description: Two-letter code of the speech; detected when left out.

level.description: Strictness instead of the account's lists: lenient (only the worst words and slurs), moderate (swearing and slurs, the default), strict (also damn, hell, crap, sexual words and taking God's name in vain), super_strict (also gosh, darn, heck and insults like stupid or shut up). Audience presets: kids (the same as super_strict), teen (swearing, slurs, sexual words and cursing with God's name; damn, hell, crap and "oh my god" stay), family (teen plus crude mild words such as crap; damn, hell and religious exclamations stay). Send level or lists, not both.

lists.description: Lists instead of the account's: profanity_mild, profanity_strong, profanity_severe, slurs, blasphemy, sexual, minced, insults, or the halves mild_damn_hell and mild_crude (of profanity_mild), blasphemy_exclamations (oh my god, jesus, good lord) and blasphemy_curses (goddamn) (of blasphemy). A half reports its parent's category. Send level or lists, not both.

words.description: More words to block, added to the account's Blocked Words. A plain word also catches its forms (rape also catches raped, raping, rapes, rapist); =word is only that exact word; word*, *word* and phrases as before.

allow.description: Words never to censor, added to the account's Never Censor list.

pad_ms.description: Silence this many ms around each word.

music.description: Loud music mode: true also listens to the voices with the music taken out, for words music hides (675 more requests a minute), and splits two voices talking at once to hear the quieter one (640 more a minute): 1,925 a minute in all, up front. The 675 comes back when the gaps between words are quiet or the pass fails (the job says music: used, not_needed or failed); of the 640, 600 for each minute with no overlap sent to recognition and all of it on a failure (the job says overlap: used, not_needed or failed). false turns it off. Left out: the account's setting.

profile.description: One of the account's named Censored profiles (censor_settings lists them; any case): its lists replace the account's, its words and allow add to them. Unknown is a 400, nothing charged.

review.description: true stops at the hit list: job_status answers status review with hits ({ id, word masked like f***, start, end, category, confidence, keep }). Change them with censor_edit_hits, then censor_render renders it, free. Same price; the review is kept 24 hours (the rendered file an hour).

audio_track.description: Which audio track to censor: its number (0 is the first, the default) or its language code (fr, fre). Every other audio and subtitle track and the chapters are kept; an mp4 leaves out codecs it can't hold (the result's dropped). An unknown track is a 400 (reason audio_track_not_found), nothing charged; with a link it is found when the file is fetched and the job fails with the charge given back.

imdb.description: The title's IMDb id (tt0111161): the account's Never Censor words for that title (set in dash.wyzie.io Censored, per title) are added to allow. Send imdb or tmdb.

tmdb.description: The title's TMDB id (603), as imdb.

ranges_file_path.description: Absolute path of a local EDL, VideoSkip .skp or censor_filter JSON (2 MB, 20000 ranges): its ranges are silenced with no speech recognition, priced as a render only (10 a started minute). Not with music or review (400 Invalid ranges_file, nothing charged); a broken line is a 400 naming it.

idempotency_key.description: Idempotency-Key for this job (1 to 100 letters, digits, _ . : -). Default: a random one per call. The same key again answers the first job (no second job, no second charge); 409 while the first still runs.

confirm.description: Must be true to start this paid job. Leave it out first: the tool answers the price and charges nothing.

tools.description: Wyzie Censored batch (Pro): up to 20 links in one call (uploads can't be batched), each its own censor_video_url job at the same price (610 requests per started minute of media (recognition 600 + render 10; charged up front, the 600 refunded on a recognition cache hit, all of it if it fails on our side), or 1,925 with loud music mode (music: true; of the extra 1,315, the voices pass's 675 and the overlap pass's 640 are given back as far as the file doesn't need them: the job says music and overlap)), charged when it starts, two at a time a key. The censor options here go to every item; an item's own win. The first refused charge (402) stops the batch: that item and the rest end skipped_no_balance, uncharged; a failed item is refunded by its own job. webhook gets one batch.done call. Without confirm: true it prices each item (dry run) and charges nothing; show it to the user, then call again with confirm: true. Poll with censor_batch_status.

tools.name: censor_batch_status
tools.description: Read a Wyzie Censored batch (free): status running, done or stopped (stopped no_balance or refused), counts, cost, charged, and each item's status (pending, running, done, failed, skipped_no_balance), its job id (job_status kind censor), media once done, cost and charged. Only the key that started it; kept 24 hours. Never starts or charges anything.

tools.name: censor_video_file
tools.description: Wyzie Censored (Pro) for a local video or audio file on this machine (up to 2 GB: a file over 100 MB is sent in resumable 8 MB chunks from disk, SHA-256 checked; or send a link to censor_video_url). tools.name: censor_filter
tools.description: A finished Wyzie Censored job's ranges as a filter file a player mutes from, so the original file stays untouched: json (default, { count, ranges: [{ start, end, action: mute, category, word }] }, seconds), edl (Kodi, MPlayer, mpv: one `start end 1` line per range; save it next to the video as <video name>.edl) or skp (VideoSkip). word is masked (f***). Only the key that started the job; 409 while it runs. Free.

tools.name: censor_subtitle
tools.description: A finished Wyzie Censored job's transcript as a subtitle with the censored words masked (f***), srt (default), vtt or txt (plain text, one cue a line). style bleep writes [bleep] (or [muted]) in place of the word; stars (default) masks it. marks: true adds a [bleep] (or [muted]) caption over each censored range. Only the key that started the job; 409 while it runs, 404 for jobs from before transcripts were kept. Free. Output is cut at 60000 characters.

tools.name: censor_edit_hits
tools.description: A Wyzie Censored job started with review: true (status review): keep or drop hits by id, and add ranges to mute (at most 500): { start, end } seconds exactly as sent, or by word place from censor_transcript: { word: i } or { from: i, to: j } (inclusive; a bad place is a 400). Answers the job, still in review, with its hits. Only the key that started it; 409 outside review. Free. Then censor_render renders the list.

add.description: More ranges to mute: { start, end } seconds, { word: i } or { from: i, to: j } (word places from censor_transcript).

tools.name: censor_transcript
tools.description: A Wyzie Censored job started with review: true (status review): its words for transcript editing, { id, state, count, words: [{ i, w, s, e, hit? }] }: i is the word's place, w the word, s and e seconds, hit the hit id when a hit covers it (covered words come masked, f***). Bleep any word with censor_edit_hits add [{ word: i }] or [{ from: i, to: j }]. Only the key that started the job, only while in review (kept 24 hours); 404 otherwise. Free. Output is cut at 60000 characters.

tools.name: censor_render
tools.description: Render a review: true Wyzie Censored job's (edited) hit list: kept hits are silenced as the job would have, added ranges exactly. Free (the job paid at its start). Once per job (409 after). Poll with job_status (kind censor); a failed render goes back to status review with error.

tools.name: censor_settings
tools.description: The Wyzie Censored settings the key runs with (on or off, lists, level: lenient, moderate, strict, super_strict, teen, family or custom (kids reads as super_strict), mode, sound, padding; counts of Blocked Words and Never Censor words, never the words) and the prices. available.levels lists each level's lists, available.languages the languages with their own preset lists. profiles: the account's named profiles ({ name, level, lists, words, allow }, word counts only) to send as profile. Free.

tools.name: job_status
tools.description: Read a Wyzie Censored job (free): processing (with its place in the queue) or done (ranges, and links to the files, valid 15 minutes and 20 downloads; the file is kept an hour; read the job again for fresh links); warnings (each name: text; names multiple_audio_tracks, surround, variable_frame_rate, quiet_audio, dropped_tracks), audio_track (the track censored) and dropped (tracks an mp4 can't hold); ledger { charged, refunded, net, reason } (reason: why it failed or refund pending: ..., else null), also printed as a Ledger line. A job started with review: true stops at status review with hits (change them with censor_edit_hits, then censor_render). wait: true keeps polling, with growing waits, until it is done or in review. save_path (when done) downloads the job's media to that local file, asking the job once for a fresh link if the link expired. Never starts or charges a job.

wait.description: Keep polling until the job is done (up to an hour).

save_path.description: Absolute path of a local file to write the finished job's media to (.mp4, .mkv, .m4a...). An existing file only with overwrite: true; inside WYZIE_MCP_ROOT when that is set.

overwrite.description: With save_path: replace an existing file.

stderr: wyzie-mcp: no WYZIE_KEY set. Tools that need a key will say how to get one (https://sub.wyzie.io/redeem).
